h: Reservoir Birds and a Marble Temple
p: Staples Corner can feel like a jumble of roads, but tucked right next to it is a surprising slice of nature. The Welsh Harp, officially the Brent Reservoir, is a large reservoir and nature reserve where you can spot waterbirds, watch sailing boats and enjoy a walk on the paths round the edge. It's a peaceful antidote to the A406 traffic.

If you're travelling by train, Brent Cross West station opened in 2023 on the Thameslink line, which gives another option for getting to this part of north-west London. Buses also run along the Edgware Road and the North Circular.

For a visit that feels a world away from a trampoline park, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Neasden is a stunning Hindu temple, hand-carved from marble and limestone. Visitors are welcome, and it's a beautiful and calm place to visit with older children, though there's a dress code, so check before you go.

Wembley Stadium is a short drive west, and even if there's no event on, the giant arch is an impressive sight. To the east, Golders Hill Park on the edge of Hampstead Heath has a small free animal enclosure, a butterfly house and lovely gardens, and the wider Heath is perfect for a long walk with views back over London from Parliament Hill.
Hendon and Golders Green have plenty of places to eat, so finding a family-friendly meal after your session is easy enough.
Staples Corner traffic can be slow at peak times, so plan ahead and give yourself a buffer if you've booked a time slot.
